transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I feel like the future has just kind of closed in on me, like there isn’t much to look forward to anymore. It's just been this constant, heavy feeling, and I finally realized I couldn't keep ignoring it.
How long have you been feeling this way, and have you experienced similar periods of feeling this low in the past?

It’s been going on pretty steadily for a little over two years now, starting a few months after my bank merged with a larger company. Before this started, I had never experienced periods of feeling this low in my life.
During these past two years, have you had any periods of feeling back to your normal self for more than two months at a time, or has this low mood been present nearly every day?

No, I haven't had any breaks at all. This low mood has been present nearly every single day without any periods of feeling like my old self. It has just been a steady, continuous struggle for the last two years.
During these past two years, have you experienced any significant symptoms like changes in your appetite, sleep patterns, or a loss of interest in activities you used to enjoy?

I've completely lost interest in the things I used to love, like hiking, pottery, and tending to my garden—now they just feel like chores or completely pointless. I haven't really noticed any major changes in my sleep or appetite, though.
Have you noticed any persistent feelings of low self-esteem, difficulty concentrating, or a sense of hopelessness during these past two years?

My self-esteem is okay, but the hopelessness is very real; it feels like my future is just grinding out work until retirement and there's no point in trying my hobbies because nothing will make me feel better. My concentration is also terrible—my mind fogs over so badly at work that I have to reread loan notes multiple times, and I even struggle with simple decisions like choosing a blouse in the morning.

Have these symptoms ever become so severe that they significantly impaired your ability to function, or have they remained at a relatively consistent, steady level of intensity throughout these two years?

They have stayed at a pretty steady, consistent level of intensity, but they have definitely taken a toll on my daily life. At work, my performance reviews have started mentioning that I seem less engaged and have missed follow-ups. Outside of work, I've pulled back from friends, hiking, and my art classes, and I just go straight home and let my house and garden slide.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks where your mood was much lower than your current baseline, accompanied by physical symptoms like significant weight loss or constant fatigue?

No, I haven't had any periods where my mood was significantly worse than this; the fatigue and low mood have just been a steady, constant baseline for the past two years. I haven't experienced any major weight loss either. It has just been this same heavy, draining feeling day in and day out since the merger.
Have you ever experienced a distinct period of at least two weeks where you felt completely unable to function, or where you had thoughts that life was not worth living?

No, I've never had thoughts that life wasn't worth living, and I haven't had a period where I was completely unable to function. It has really just been this steady, heavy drag over the last two years rather than any kind of sudden, severe breakdown.
